label: copy-phase input p (fed-back p) from recall position 3 on
explanation: Token detector for the letter p used as a fed-back input during the copy phase. More than 99% of steps where it is active have in_tok == p, and it never fires in the original or delimiter phases. It is mostly silent when p comes back early in the copy (recall_idx <= 2, meaning p was original token 0 or 1): the firing rate starts at recall_idx 2 and levels off at recall_idx >= 3. Activations are weakest at the earliest positions (bottom-quartile examples are p fed back at recall_idx 2-3), and the strongest ones (about 0.95-1.0 of max) are p fed back with few outputs left. Most false positives are p at original position 2 in long sequences (L=7-9). It does not fire on p in the original sequence or on any other token, and the output token has no effect.

issues: The core claims hold. The feature only fires in the copy phase (0 active steps in the original or delimiter phases). Of the copy-phase activations, 56681/57069 have in_tok == p; the predicate (phase==2)&(in_tok!=p) has precision 0.00015. The output token has no effect: the out_tok rates are flat at about 0.019.

The fixed cutoff recall_idx >= 3 is wrong at the edges, and the error depends on sequence length. It is not scattered noise. (1) At recall_idx==2 the feature fires reliably when L<=4: precision 0.92 at L=4 and 1.00 at L=3. It is almost silent when L>=5 (0.015 at L=5, 0.0 at L>=6). So the claim that it is mostly silent when recall_idx<=2 is wrong for short sequences, where that step is one of the last outputs. (2) At recall_idx==3 precision is 0.99 for L<=6 but only 0.72, 0.45 and 0.53 for L=7, 8 and 9. This is the false-positive class the explanation names, and the predicate does not handle it.

The rule is roughly 'fires on fed-back p once enough of the copy is done': it fires at recall_idx>=4 for every L (precision 1.00), at recall_idx 3 only when L<=7, and at recall_idx 2 only when L<=4. The explanation says that trying to cover sequences with few outputs left did not help. A predicate with these length-dependent thresholds does help: test F1 rises from 0.940 to 0.963, precision from 0.935 to 0.981, and missed activation mass falls from 2.0% to 0.7%.

The remaining misses on the test split are very weak activations (0.00-0.09 of max) on p at recall_idx 2-3 in L=8 sequences, plus a few boundary cases. The remaining false positives are near-threshold p at recall_idx 2 (L=4) and recall_idx 3 (L=7). This is scattered noise at the boundary.
The label 'from recall position 3 on' slightly overclaims: at recall_idx 3 with L>=7 the feature fires only about half the time, and the label leaves out recall_idx 2 in short sequences (L<=4).
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase fed-back p once enough of the copy is done (recall_idx>=4; recall_idx 3 if L<=7; recall_idx 2 if L<=4)
